sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r16/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks sheet row 36 = check 35; Internal Quality Checks sheet row 36; no cell comments on the row)
evidence:
DEFINING BEHAVIOUR IS GRADED. The product is a custom code editor + Run/preview + saved revisions (instruction.md). Functional judge.toml grades each directly with positive controls: editing (cw_custom_typing_and_line_join l.23 onward, multi-caret, find/replace, format), running (cw_basic_run_output l.212-219: 'Press Run: the preview must show the correct sum and the app console must contain it', then edit and re-run so a canned output cannot pass; cw_html_preview; error/stop/time-limit criteria), and saving (l.338 onward). The render gate only checks load-and-type, so a dead Run is excluded by scored criteria, not by the gate; that is consistent with REVIEW_POLICY 'Keep unrelated difficulty in scored outcomes'.

STATE DURABILITY IS PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED. (1) Reload with client storage excluded: constraints gate cw_shared_saved_record (all_pass gate) and functional cw_save_reload_restart both say 'clear this origin's browser storage as described in the application notes and reload', and app_context.md enumerates 'localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB databases, Cache Storage, the origin private file system, service worker registrations and cookies'. A localStorage/IndexedDB-only app therefore fails the gate (reward 0), which satisfies REVIEW_POLICY 'Gates must exclude convincing dead apps'. (2) Process restart: cw_save_reload_restart l.344 'call the verifier-provided restart_app tool once. After it reports a completed restart, a fresh page must show the same single record with the same revision, title, filename, source and the same list of revisions in its history ... Do not infer a restart from a reload or a health response'; functional/prompt.md 'Restart evidence' section restricts the tool to that criterion. The tool is real: judge.toml l.14-18 wires the verifier MCP server to /tests/tools/restart_mcp.py with $APP_RESTART_HELPER; test.sh writes app-restart.sh which kills the process group and relaunches the same entry with the same DB_PATH. test.sh and restart_mcp.py are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff clean). An in-memory server store fails here. (3) Shared across pages: cw_stale_save_refused, cw_stale_save_keeps_draft ('a fresh read of the record in a third page'), cw_live_library_update and cw_restore_request_repeat_safe ('a freshly loaded page must show exactly three revisions') read state back from a different or freshly loaded page. No accounts exist, so re-auth is N-A (app_context.md 'Accounts: None').

SERVER-BACKED vs SAME-ORIGIN. The criteria do not accept 'same origin responded' as proof; they require storage-cleared readback plus a real process restart on the same database. A browser judge cannot prove SQLite specifically (REVIEW_POLICY: 'A browser exchange cannot prove SQLite'); with a public network a submission persisting to a remote third-party store would be indistinguishable. That is an inherent limit of the browser-only judge, recorded as a note, not a defect of this task.

MEASURED EVIDENCE. Evidence-index hashes verified for restart.json (2ec1b980...), persist-before.json (19cac1c5...), persist-after.json (56b98b0a...), persist.cjs (7da3be77...) and the hosted scored/reward-details.json LF-normalised (bacbf94c...). Scripted golden on these bytes: persist-before cw_shared_saved_record true and cw_save_reload_restart(before) true; persist-after cw_save_reload_restart true after one real process restart; restart.json shows record id 3 revision 2 history [2,1] read back. Hosted configured-judge run on an EARLIER candidate: cw_save_reload_restart value 1.0 with reasoning quoting the tool reply 'restart complete: the server was relaunched on the same database and answers HTTP', which shows the restart tool wiring (unchanged, template-identical) works under the configured judge. No configured judge run exists for these exact bytes, and the restart criterion wording changed since that run (marker typed mid-line, 'same list of revisions'); that missing measurement is why risk=true.

NOTES (not blocking for this row). N1: the restart proof of history is thin. behaviour.md says 'saved work and history must survive a complete server restart' and integration.md 'Keep the same records and revision history after a process restart', but cw_save_reload_restart says 'Save once', so the history compared across the restart has exactly one entry and only the list of revisions, not an older revision's content, is compared. A weak app that persists only the current snippet row in SQLite and keeps earlier revisions in process memory (rebuilding a one-entry history from the current row at start-up) passes every criterion: multi-revision history is only ever read back from freshly loaded pages of the same process (cw_history_restore_adds_revision, cw_restore_request_repeat_safe), never after the restart, and the restart tool is single use. The scripted golden test is stronger than the criterion (revision 2, history [2,1]). Suggested tightening: in cw_save_reload_restart save twice with different sources before the restart and, after it, open revision one in history and confirm its source. N2: the restart helper (template-controlled test.sh) sends SIGTERM to the process group, waits at most five seconds and never escalates; probe_ready then accepts any HTTP answer on port 3000. A submission that deliberately ignores SIGTERM keeps its old process, the relaunch dies on the busy port, and the tool still reports 'restart complete', so an in-memory store would pass. This needs a deliberately hostile app and lives in shared harness code that must not be edited for QC; recorded only. N3: playwright-mcp tabs share one browser context, so 'independent browser contexts' (integration.md) is proven through storage clearing plus fresh pages rather than a truly separate context; a same-tab window.name stash is the only client-side channel the clearing list omits, and it does not survive the fresh page after restart or reach the third page in cw_stale_save_*.
suggested_fix: Optional hardening for N1: in cw_save_reload_restart, Save twice with different sources before calling restart_app, then after the restart require both revisions listed and revision one's source shown exactly when inspected.
